items.question: What is the difference between a primary-market sale and a secondary-market trade?
items.answer: In the primary market, an issuer sells newly issued securities and receives the money. In the secondary market, investors trade existing securities with one another; the seller receives the money.

items.question: What is an ETF? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: An exchange-traded fund: a pooled investment fund whose shares trade on an exchange during the trading day. Chinese: 交易所交易基金.

items.question: A worker puts money into a 401(k) and buys an S&P 500 index fund. Identify the account, investment vehicle, benchmark and underlying assets.
items.answer: The 401(k) is the retirement account or plan; the index fund is the investment vehicle; the S&P 500 is the benchmark; the underlying assets are shares of the companies held by the fund.

items.question: What right does a call option give its buyer? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: The right, but not the obligation, to buy the underlying asset at the strike price under the contract's rules. Chinese: 看涨期权.

items.question: What right does a put option give its buyer? Give its Simplified Chinese equivalent.
items.answer: The right, but not the obligation, to sell the underlying asset at the strike price under the contract's rules. Chinese: 看跌期权.

items.question: Why can a call-option buyer lose money even if the stock price rises?
items.answer: The stock may not rise above the strike price plus the premium by expiration. A small rise can leave the option worth less than the premium paid; time and volatility also affect the option's price.
